correctness.rationale: For m,n>=3 graph-distance layers are exactly 1 and 2, plus a unique distance-3 missed partner of a matched root. No successful game can empty its target; partition initial cups by their final transfers into the target. Each packet holding an A-side cup other than a root in A contains a B-side cup; the sole possible distance-3 packet additionally can hold at most two A-side cups. The sharp necessary inequality m-1<=n+1_{matched} follows. The sufficiency proof constructs one 3-cup packet at the missed partner when matched and saturating 2-cup packets by a proved Hall matching fact; all legal moves and the symmetric B case are explicit. Independent brute-force state search matched every target classification on 346 cases, 666192 memoized states counted across cases; the constructive verifier executed 6984 valid sequences. These are finite checks only, not infinite certification.

originality.rationale: The 2023 complete-multipartite criterion is the t=0 baseline and the eccentricity-two matching lemma does not reach a matched endpoint (eccentricity three). The 2024 Hamilton-path theorem covers many globally stackable graphs, but cannot imply the new successful targets on bipartite G_{n+2,n,t}, which has no Hamilton path because its sides differ by two. The 2024 rooted K_{a,b} theorem explicitly says the larger-side roots fail for t=0; deleting one incident edge yields a sharp opposite outcome. Targeted literature and published-claim-index searches under cup stacking, crown graphs, deleted matchings, frog jumping, and aliases did not identify the full rooted profile. Residual independent/unindexed overlap is possible.
residual_risks: Earlier or unindexed geodesic frog-jumping results could use a different title/notation.
No claim is made about all graph families, initial configurations, or all successful sequences.
Publication search cannot prove global absence of an equivalent theorem.

value.rationale: Root feasibility is an intrinsically defined goal of the original cup-stacking game, and deleting disjoint matching edges is a canonical controlled perturbation of complete bipartite graphs. The complete three-parameter theorem has a sharp, nontrivial +2 versus +1 threshold, explicit efficient witnesses, and a natural one-edge non-Hamiltonian target-flip family absent from the known complete-bipartite rooted classification. This identifies the function of the new distance-3 packet, not a routine restatement of a general bound.
